targetWords.definition: To cherish something means to hold it as very important.
targetWords.example: I cherish this trophy I won. C O m p a S S iO t l [kampsejan] n.

targetWords.definition: — The veterinarian had compassion for the sick little puppy.
Consent is permission to do something.
targetWords.example: Their mother gave the children consent to go outside and play.

targetWords.definition: The core is the center of something.
targetWords.example: The rings of a tree start forming at its core.

targetWords.definition: If someone is cunning, they are good at tricking people. — The cunning child fooled his parents into thinking that he was kind.
If someone is dizzy, then they feel off balance as if they will fall down.
targetWords.example: The pregnant woman was dizzy after standing up too quickly.

targetWords.definition: Equilibrium is the balance between different forces.
targetWords.example: The sudden drop in prices upset the equilibrium of the economy.

targetWords.definition: To foster a feeling or a skill means to help it develop.
targetWords.example: She helped foster a sense of calm in the little boy.

targetWords.definition: To grind something means to break it into very small pieces or powder.
targetWords.example: She wanted to grind the beans, so she could brew some coffee.

targetWords.definition: To growl means to make a deep, angry sound.
targetWords.example: The dog started to growl at the man walking by.

targetWords.definition: It is important to eat in moderation so that you can have a healthy body. predator [predatar] n.
— The peregrine falcon is a predator that eats fish.
If someone is sane, they can think in a normal way.
targetWords.example: Oliver does not act like a sane person when he is angry. saucer [so.sar] n.

targetWords.definition: — He placed the spoon on the saucer.
To snatch something means to take it away with a quick motion.
targetWords.example: He was so hungry that he snatched an apple from a tree.

targetWords.definition: He staggered around after having too much to drink.
To stumble means to put your foot down wrong so that you almost fall.
targetWords.example: He stumbled as he ran through the puddle.

targetWords.definition: If someone is tense, they are worried something bad might happen.
targetWords.example: After the phone call, Monica was very tense. tumble [tAmbal] V. To tumble means to fall, often in a rolling way.

targetWords.definition: To withhold something is to not give it to someone.
targetWords.example: They withheld all information until she paid her fine.

story.title: M U The
story.passage:
A traveler stopped at an inn. He sat and watched people closely, like a predator. He

heard the old innkeeper talking to a young man in the core of the inn.

"I just need to borrow some money. I swear that I'll spend it in moderation, and my

friend will pay you back tomorrow," the man said. The innkeeper gave his consent and

pulled out some money.

The traveler knew that this was a trick. The man was going

to leave with the poor innkeeper's money and never return.

He felt compassion for the nice innkeeper and did not want

him to be tricked. The cunning traveler decided to teach the

innkeeper a lesson.

The traveler walked over to the innkeeper and sat down.

The innkeeper had started to grind coffee beans to make

coffee. He made the coffee and handed the traveler a

saucer and a cup. The two started talking. After a while the

traveler yawned and then growled like a wolf.

"Are you not sane? I thought I just heard you growl,"

said the innkeeper.

"I did. I am cursed. Every time I yawn three times in a row,

I turn into a wolf and attack people."

The innkeeper became tense. Then the traveler yawned again. As the

traveler started to yawn a third time, the innkeeper turned to run outside. As he

ran, the traveler snatched his coat. The scared innkeeper staggered outside and tumbled

into the street.

The traveler followed him out because he did not want to withhold the truth any longer.

He just wanted to foster happiness and restore the innkeeper's emotional equilibrium.

The innkeeper was dizzy, and he stumbled. The traveler helped him stand up.

"That was a trick," the traveler said as he

returned the coat.

"Oh, good. I cherish this coat," responded

the innkeeper.

"Well, hopefully this will teach you that

you shouldn't believe every story that you

hear."
